question: How grave is the fault of destroying a woman according to the Ratnamala?
premises: The Ratnamala addresses the case of transgressing a vow.
Destroying a woman is described as a great fault.
The consequence stated is everlasting hell.
inference: The text treats violence against a woman as an exceptionally severe transgression not covered by ordinary expiation.
uncertainties: The term 'śakti' is read here as 'woman' in line with the context, though it can have other senses elsewhere.
plain_english: In the revered Ratnamala, when a vow has been transgressed, it is said: from destroying a woman comes a great fault and everlasting hell, O beloved.
